To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the photoelectrochemical degradation efficiency of emerging organic pollutants can be enhanced when compared with photocatlytic degradation alone, and this is achieved by the use of metal oxide nanocomposites as photoactive materials.
metal oxides nanocomposites are efficient photocatalytic materials that are able to degrade pharmaceutical pollutants in aqueous solutions.

the combination of adsorption and photoelectrochemical processes using metal oxide nanocomposites is an effective method for removal and mineralization of emerging organic compounds in aqueous solutions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the removal of organic pollutants from aqueous solution using photocatalysis and photoelectrocatalytic processes.
the development of novel nanocomposites for the removal of emerging organic pollutants from aqueous solution.
the synthesis of metal oxide nanocomposites for the adsorption and photoelectrocatalytic removal of pharmaceutical pollutants in aqueous solution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
photocatalysis is an effective technique to remove emerging organic pollutants, but photoelectrocatalytic oxidation is a much more effective technique for mineralising emerging organic pollutants.
the application of photoelectroclysis using semiconducting materials is more efficient than the application of photocatalysis alone.
photoelectrocatalytic degradation of emerging organic pollutants in aqueous solution is a very effective process that can be used as a remediation tool.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the photoelectrocatalytic degradation is more efficient than photocatalysis alone for the degradation of pharmaceuticals and this is attributed to the special separation of photoinduced electron hole pair.
photoelectrocatalytic degradation using metal oxide nanocomposites is a promising and viable technique for the removal of pharmaceutical pollutants.
photoelectrocatalytic degradation of organic pollutants in water using metal oxide nanocomposites is a promising technology for the removal of organic pollutants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
photoelectrocatalytic systems are more effective than photocatalytic systems for the removal of organic pollutants.
photoelectrocatalysts are more efficient in mineralising organic pollutants than photocatalysts alone.
the efficiency of the photocatalysis is enhanced when an external field is applied across the catalyst and that the degradation is enhanced when the catalyst is doped with metal oxides.
